Every part in the palette, in the palette’s order: what it is, its settings with their defaults, and its signals. This chapter is generated from the page’s own part definitions when the book is built, so it lists exactly what v2.02 has.

A signal’s alias tag is the part’s name and the signal’s, joined by an underscore: a diffuse sensor named LS1 has the signal Detect, so its alias is LS1_Detect (chapter 5). Digital in and analog in are inputs to the controller (the part tells the program something); digital out and analog out are outputs (the program tells the part to do something). Signals marked with … appear only when that setting is ticked or chosen.

Revolver Feeder

rotary magazine: spins and feeds

A rotary magazine like a revolver cylinder: Pockets bores round a drum beside the lane, loaded with Parts loaded at start. A rising edge on Index turns the drum one pocket (Index time) and the part that reaches the drop pocket lands on the lane; InPosition is 1 while the drum stands still, PartReady while a part sits in the drop pocket with the lane clear, Empty when the drum has run out. Reload (or Reload by itself) refills every pocket in about a second. Pair it with a sensor on the lane: XIC(PartReady) XIO(Lane_Eye) OSR → Index is the classic one-at-a-time feed.

Vision

Vision Sensor

Recognises the part under it. Digital: one BOOL per ticked part. Bits: the part code as five binary inputs Bit0-Bit4 (Factory I/O's "All Digital"). Numerical: one INT with the part code (the number next to each part in the list; 0 = none or not ticked). ID: the serial number of the part in view plus its code, usable like a barcode. Size: the older Small/Medium/Large/Metal outputs. Tick Triggered for a Trigger output with Busy and Complete, like a real smart camera: the result then holds until the next trigger. Set Inspection job to Bottle inspection and it checks a bottle's cap, label and fill instead: Pass is a bottle with all three, and on a camera module the result code is bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill, bit 3 no part in view, with the fill in % of the label in byte 9 of Inspection_Results. On a camera module, Buffer_Results_Enable queues results up to the buffer depth until the PLC acknowledges each one (Results_Buffer_Overrun when one is lost). A Process HMI set to show the sensor draws its camera screen. Card mode (bottle job): the bottle cards SN-4801 to SN-4804 decide each bottle. The hopper sends plain good bottles; when a result comes back, the bottle under the camera takes the card's verdict (no cap, no label, short fill; no card in view makes it a reject) and moves on. Each bottle waits at the camera until its result is presented, so there is time to swap the card. With the simulated camera, pick the card in Card under the lens or on the camera screen's CARDS page; with the camera module live on a real In-Sight, the real card decides: its result code, the fill in byte 9 and the card ID in byte 10 of Inspection_Results.

  • LED: Green: a part in view. Amber: result valid for a selected part. The ring light flashes on a trigger.
  • Detects: Every part in the catalogue; tick the ones to detect.

Code Reader

DataMan 260 series, EtherNet/IP

A fixed-mount code reader of the Cognex DataMan 260 series (the DM262 and kin) on EtherNet/IP. It has no wired signals: it works on its module's tags. Type the module's name into Reader module, or use Add DataMan Module in its properties. The handshake is the reader's own: set Trigger_Enable; a 0 → 1 on Trigger with Trigger_Ready on takes an image (hold Trigger until Trigger_Ack); after the decode time Results_Available comes on with Result_ID (the trigger it answers), Result_Code (bit 0 = read, bit 1 = matches the match string), Result_Length and the string in Result_Data; set Results_Ack and drop it once Results_Available clears. Buffer_Results_Enable queues results until each is acknowledged; a result that finds the queue full is lost and Results_Buffer_Overrun says so. A trigger while it is busy is missed (Missed_Acq, and bit 3 on the next result). SoftEvent 1 trains the match string from the next read, 4 clears it, 7 sets it from User_Data. Add Example Routine writes a routine with the whole handshake. Click the reader in Run mode for its screen. Implicit mode: the module talks to your reader through the bridge and the part shows what the real reader decoded.

Drives & Axes

Linear Axis

axis and servo motor; its drive is the Festo FHPP module

Three things make a servo axis: the axis (a toothed-belt or spindle profile with a carriage: the part), the servo motor on its end (drawn with it) and the drive, the servo controller in the cabinet, which is the module in I/O Configuration. The PLC talks to the drive over EtherNet/IP with the FHPP profile: eight bytes each way. Out: CCON (Enable, Stop, Brake, Reset, Lock, OPM1/2), CPOS (Halt, Start, Home, Jog_Pos, Jog_Neg, Teach, Clear), Record_No, Setpoint_Vel, Setpoint_Pos. In: SCON (Enabled, Op_Enabled, Warning, Fault …), SPOS (Halt_Ack, Start_Ack, Motion_Complete, Teach_Ack, Moving, Drag_Error, Standstill, Referenced), Record_No, Actual_Vel, Actual_Pos (0.01 mm). The part has no wired signals: type its module's name into Axis module, or press Add Axis Module. The handshake is the real one: Enable + Stop give operation enabled; Home is the only move before the axis is referenced; Start runs the record (or the Direct-mode setpoint, OPM1 = 1) on its rising edge, and Motion_Complete drops until the target is reached; Halt low pauses a task and Start resumes it, Clear drops it; a Start while moving is ignored with Warning; a Start before homing, an unset record or a target past the stroke is a fault only Reset clears. Jog moves while held and stops at the ends; Teach writes the actual position into the record. Stroke, speeds and records are the part's properties; the axis is drawn to scale (60 px per metre). Gripper puts a vacuum gripper on the carriage: Grip rising lifts the part under the carriage and it rides along, unseen by eyes, belts and bins; Grip falling sets it down where the carriage is (a bin, a belt, or the floor); Gripped and Part_Below report. Axis size picks the profile (Festo builds them in sizes 45 to 185 mm wide, toothed belt or ball-screw spindle): it sets the drawn width, the stroke range and the velocity and acceleration ceiling, and a setting past the ceiling is held at it. The figures are typical of a catalogue, not of one drive: check the axis you buy. On a live module the part follows the real drive's Actual_Pos.

A healthy idle axis shows EN, REF and MC lit and ERR dark; EN alone means not yet homed; EN and REF without MC means it is moving; ERR means read the reason under the carriage (FAULT: …) or the full line in the Simulator Log tab, then press Reset. The readout is the actual position.

VFD

variable frequency drive, hardwired: 0-10 V speed reference

A variable frequency drive wired to the controller the way most are: two-wire Run (and Rev) from digital outputs, a 0-10 V speed reference from an analog output channel, and Ready, Running, AtSpeed and Fault back to digital inputs, plus its analog output (OutputFreq) for the actual frequency. The analog channels are in engineering units, 0-10000 = 0-10.000 V, and 10 V is the Frequency at 10 V setting, so a reference of 5000 asks for 30 Hz on a 60 Hz drive: scale it in the program (SCP or CPT). A trip (Tools → Inject Machine Fault) switches the output off and latches until the cause is gone and FaultReset rises. To put it on a conveyor, type its name in the belt's Driven by drive module: the belt then runs at its Speed × output frequency ÷ the 10 V frequency, and its own Fwd output is not used.

Elevator

The classic elevator scene, a panoramic lift. The cab rides between two and six floors on its hoist: Up and Down move it a floor per Travel time; both together do nothing, the contactors are interlocked. At_N is the floor switch, made while the cab is level; Encoder is the shaft encoder, 1000 counts a floor (floor 1 = 1000). A stop inside the door zone levels the cab. The door: Open and Close run it in Door travel time; Door_Open and Door_Closed are its end switches; the landing doors part with it. Door_Eye is blocked while a passenger stands in the doorway, and a Close then does not close. Call_N and Cab_N are the buttons, 1 while pressed (a passenger presses for 0.3 s; click the call plates and cab buttons yourself). Lamp_N lights the call plate and the cab button of a floor, Ind_N the displays. Passengers arrive on their own at the rate set, board at their floor with the door fully open, press a cab button, ride and leave; one who waits 45 s is lost. Overload is five riders. Moving with the door open is allowed and counted as unsafe: on a real elevator the door contact is in the safety chain and the hoist cannot run; here that is your program's job, so you can see what the chain is for.
